title: Search a 2D Matrix
source: canonical Search a 2D Matrix concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is a matrix: a list of rows, where each row is a list of integers sorted ascending. The rows are stacked so that the first value of every row is larger than the last value of the row above it. Return True when target appears somewhere in the matrix, False otherwise.
constraints: each row starts above the previous row ends

examples.explanation: 13 falls between the rows: too big for row 0, too small for row 1.

hints: The stacking rule means reading the rows back to back produces one sorted list.
A position in that imagined list converts to a cell: row = position // width, column = position % width.
Run one binary search over positions 0 to rows * cols - 1, converting each midpoint to its cell value.
solution: Treat the matrix as one sorted list of rows times cols values and binary search it, converting each midpoint to a cell with division and remainder. O(log(m*n)) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include one row, one column, and targets falling between rows

visible.failNote: check where the target could live across the whole stack
a target between rows is absent
